macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Trump Media cancels two Crypto.com deals, sending CRO to a three-year low
items.summary: Trump Media said it will terminate two major agreements with Crypto.com, and CRO fell below $0.05 for the first time since late 2023. The move was one of the sharpest price reactions in the past day and stood out as a major market-moving headline.

items.title: U.S. Treasury sanctions two Iran-linked crypto exchanges
items.summary: The Treasury’s OFAC imposed sanctions on two crypto exchanges accused of helping Iran move funds and evade sanctions. This is one of the most significant regulatory developments in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Circle expands USDC into the OKX ecosystem with X Layer launch
items.summary: Circle announced an expansion of USDC support into OKX’s X Layer ecosystem. The move is a notable stablecoin and infrastructure development with potential implications for liquidity and payments activity.

items.title: Japan FSA asks exchanges to add withdrawal delays and stronger controls
items.summary: Japanese regulators urged crypto exchanges to introduce withdrawal delays, address registration, customer-specific limits, and stronger authentication to reduce scam-related abuse. The guidance reflects a broader tightening of compliance expectations in Japan.

items.title: Russia cracks down on nine unregistered crypto exchanges in Moscow City
items.summary: Russian authorities shut down nine unregistered crypto exchanges in Moscow City, alleging they were used to move scam proceeds abroad. The enforcement action adds to the day’s regulatory and anti-money-laundering headlines.

items.title: CLARITY Act delay weighs on XRP
items.summary: Reports said the U.S. crypto regulatory bill was postponed again, with the CLARITY Act possibly delayed until the midterm elections. XRP was reported to have dropped toward $1.00 as traders reacted to the delay.

items.title: Grayscale files amendment that could let its Ethereum staking mini ETF stake nearly all holdings
items.summary: Grayscale’s amended filing for its Ethereum Staking Mini ETF would reportedly allow nearly all of the fund’s ETH to be staked, with cash rewards distributed quarterly. The proposal is a significant product-development story for Ethereum investment vehicles.

items.title: Solana governance proposal could sharply increase SOL burns
items.summary: A Solana governance proposal merged on July 20, 2026, would raise daily SOL token burns from about 650 to as much as 7,500-9,000 SOL. If implemented, the change would materially increase the network’s token burn rate.

items.title: Coldcard exploit and large BTC theft remain a major security story
items.summary: Multiple reports said a Coldcard-related exploit led to more than $100 million in losses and at least 1,719 BTC stolen, with some estimates suggesting total losses could be higher. This remained one of the most important Bitcoin security stories in the period.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF flows and accumulation remain strong
items.summary: BlackRock’s IBIT reportedly withdrew 1,840 BTC from Coinbase Prime, and cumulative weekly purchases reached 7,320 BTC valued at about $478.5 million. This points to continued institutional accumulation despite mixed market sentiment.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly slows Astra model development over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: OpenAI said it has suspended work on some aspects of its upcoming Astra model because of concerns about its cybersecurity capabilities, making safety a central issue in frontier-model development. Reuters also reported OpenAI flagged a possible critical cybersecurity risk in the model and tightened controls.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Code, an AI coding agent for large code bases
items.summary: Meta released Muse Code, a dedicated coding agent aimed at helping developers work across large repositories. The launch puts Meta directly into the competitive autonomous-coding race against OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT access with unlimited text chats for free users
items.summary: OpenAI said free and Go users will get unlimited text chats, along with a new think button for more complex queries. The change broadens access while signaling continued product pressure in the consumer AI market.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a browser designed specifically for AI agents rather than human browsing alone. The move reflects a growing trend toward infrastructure and tools optimized for agentic workflows.

items.title: Cloudflare raises forecast as AI-driven enterprise spending boosts demand
items.summary: Cloudflare shares jumped after the company raised its annual forecast, citing stronger enterprise spending on AI infrastructure. The result underscores how AI demand is increasingly benefiting networking and security providers.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly plans up to $3 billion investment in Stargate data center developer Lancium
items.summary: Reuters reported that Nvidia may invest as much as $3 billion in Lancium, a developer tied to the Stargate data center project. The deal highlights continuing capital spending around AI compute infrastructure.

items.title: DeepSeek raises API prices after huge token demand
items.summary: DeepSeek reportedly increased API prices across its services after extreme demand, including processing 8 trillion tokens in a single day. The move suggests that even low-cost AI providers are facing rising compute pressure.

items.title: NVIDIA launches Nemotron 3 Ultra open-weight model
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550-billion-parameter open-weight model available through NVIDIA NIM, Hugging Face, and other inference platforms. Early benchmarks indicate it trails some leading rivals, but the launch adds another major open-weight model to the market.

items.title: Google DeepMind leadership shakeup raises questions about AI strategy
items.summary: Reports say Demis Hassabis became Alphabet chief scientist and chair while Jeff Dean departed after 27 years, prompting concern about possible delays in Gemini progress. The personnel changes are being read as an important signal about Google’s AI priorities.

items.title: OpenAI’s upcoming smart speaker reportedly priced at $300 to $400
items.summary: Multiple reports say OpenAI’s first consumer AI device may be a $300-$400 smart speaker, adding to speculation about its hardware strategy. The product would place OpenAI in direct competition with Amazon, Google, and other voice-assistant ecosystems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA is reportedly fully acquired and going private
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Electronic Arts has been fully acquired by a trio of investor groups, known as the “Consortium,” and is now a private company. This is one of the biggest gaming industry developments in the latest coverage.

items.title: Take-Two says GTA 6 preorders are off to an exceptional start
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Take-Two described Grand Theft Auto VI preorders as an “exceptional start,” despite Rockstar pricing the standard edition at $79.99. The game is still scheduled for a November 19, 2026 release.

items.title: Quake gets a free new expansion
items.summary: The Verge reports that Quake has received a new free expansion, adding fresh content to the classic shooter’s remastered release. This is one of the clearest game-update stories in the latest gaming coverage.

items.title: Minecraft is coming to Switch 2 in October
items.summary: The Verge reports that Minecraft will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 in October. The announcement adds another major title to the new console’s release lineup.

items.title: Lies of P launches on Switch 2 in full edition
items.summary: GameMAG reports that Lies of P is now available on Switch 2 in its complete edition. The release broadens the game’s platform reach to Nintendo’s new hardware.

items.title: Microsoft releases a free Quake update for the franchise’s 30th anniversary
items.summary: GameMAG reports that Microsoft has released a free update for the Quake remaster called Quake: Dawn of the Machine. The update was announced to mark the franchise’s 30th anniversary.

items.title: Game industry layoffs and restructuring continue at Xbox-related studios
items.summary: GameMAG reports that Microsoft has begun another restructuring phase affecting Halo Studios after the release of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Separate coverage in VGTimes also says an id Software lead criticized Xbox after recent layoffs, saying AAA development at the studio’s past level has become essentially impossible.

items.title: New gaming hardware supply concerns emerge around Switch 2
items.summary: DualShockers reports that Nintendo pulled Switch 2 from official stores in Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto on launch day, raising supply concerns. This appears to be a notable hardware and retail development.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.
